scope.selector: the fixed original-leaf set F(T,p)={v: Delta_p(T-v)<0}
scope.tagging: one separate tag per original leaf, including equal-support leaves

proved_counting_facts.name: earlier_layer_extension_count
proved_counting_facts.proof: Count pairs (B,z) where |B|=x and z can be added. Each independent (x+1)-set contributes its x+1 deletions.

proved_counting_facts.name: strict_descent_average
proved_counting_facts.guards: Delta_x(T)<0 implies i_x(T)>0; x+2<=p implies x+1<=k.

proved_counting_facts.name: sufficient_transfer
proved_counting_facts.formula: E=sum_{v in F} sum_{A in I_k(H_v), A meets W_v} e_{H_v}(A) <= E_x(T)*Q, where Q=sum_{v in F} q_v(k)
proved_counting_facts.consequence: Using the tagged bipartite identity from SOLUTION-CONTRACT.md, this implies S(T,p)<=0. If Q>0 it implies S(T,p)<0; if Q=0 it implies S(T,p)<=0.
proved_counting_facts.status: conditional only; universal antecedent not established

proved_counting_facts.name: tagged_bipartite_identity_proof
proved_counting_facts.proof: Count marked independent k-set/addable-vertex pairs. Extensions with exactly one W-vertex have k tag-preserving deletions; extensions with at least two W-vertices have k+1, giving k*q_(k+1)+C. In each bipartition class the addable vertices together with the original k-set form an independent set, so each class has at most h-k addables; hence e(A)<=2(h-k) and D>=0.
proved_counting_facts.scope: finite bipartite H, arbitrary marked W, h=alpha(H), 1<=k<=h

exact_bipartite_component_recipe.actual_addability: e_G(A union B)=|L\N(B)|+|R_A|-j for B subset R_A, |A|+|B|=j
exact_bipartite_component_recipe.marked_count_filter: for H_v retain only A union B intersect W_v nonempty at j=k; count each original leaf v separately

limitations: The transfer inequality is not proved universally.
No claim about recovery or unimodality is made.
No census, literature theorem, or counterexample was used.
